real_name_composite: PLA Western Theatre Command — responsible for Ladakh, Doklam, Arunachal frontier; commanded by General Wang Haijiang during Galwan (2020)

real_life_notes.western_theatre_command: Established 2016 under PLA reorganisation; headquartered in Chengdu; covers India frontier, Tibet Military District, and Central Asian borders.
real_life_notes.galwan_authorization: The Galwan ambush (June 15, 2020) was pre-planned: iron rods, barbed-wire clubs were prepared in advance. Indian intelligence assessed this required Theatre Command authorisation minimum — likely CMC awareness.
real_life_notes.doklam_creep: The same command directed the road construction at Doklam (2017) that triggered the 73-day standoff. The Doklam→Galwan escalation ladder shows a consistent doctrine of territorial salami-slicing.

objective: Execute territorial expansion along LAC through incremental boundary creep (salami-slicing); exploit India-Pakistan two-front pressure windows; deny Siliguri Corridor proximity to India; establish permanent forward positions pre-Galwan status quo
oracle_threat_note: Film 4's second-front adversary. Highest capability (10.0) in the oracle dataset. Unlike ISI, PLA operates on a 10-20 year strategic horizon — individual incidents are subordinate to territorial consolidation doctrine. Galwan was both a tactical ambush and a strategic message about the two-front threat.
